name: Yüan Mei
bio: Yüan Mei was a Ch’ing poet and critic. His poem here is a sceptical epigram on the gods.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Scoffer
poems.author: Yüan Mei
poems.text:
I've ever thought it passing odd
How all men reverence some God,
And wear their lives out for his sake
And bow their heads until they ache.
'Tis clear to me the Gods are made
Of the same stuff as wind or shade

Ah, if they came to every caller,
I'd be the very loudest bawler!
